input.content:
# Summarize the most common cell-cell communication patterns from the RaCInG kernel output
# (Gide cohort). Inputs: racing_inputs/result.rds, racing_kernel/result.rds,
# sample_id_mapping.csv. Run from the results/ directory.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(ggplot2); library(pheatmap) })

out_dir <- "patterns"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

inputs <- readRDS("racing_inputs/result.rds")
kern <- readRDS("racing_kernel/result.rds")
map <- read.csv("sample_id_mapping.csv")

feat <- as.matrix(kern$features)
rownames(feat) <- map$original[match(rownames(feat), map$racing_id)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(rownames(feat)))
write.csv(feat, file.path(out_dir, "Gide_direct_communication_features.csv"))

# ---- map every feature to its two cell types -------------------------------------------
ct <- inputs$celltypes
pairs <- expand.grid(i = seq_along(ct), j = seq_along(ct))
pairs <- pairs[pairs$i <= pairs$j, ]
pairs$feature <- paste0("Dir_", ct[pairs$i], "_", ct[pairs$j])
pairs$feature_rev <- paste0("Dir_", ct[pairs$j], "_", ct[pairs$i])
idx <- match(colnames(feat), pairs$feature)
idx_rev <- match(colnames(feat), pairs$feature_rev)
idx[is.na(idx)] <- idx_rev[is.na(idx)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(idx))
cell_a <- ct[pairs$i[idx]]
cell_b <- ct[pairs$j[idx]]

# Cell-type label (subgroups -> their cell type; single features -> method_signature_<cell>)
label_of <- function(x) ifelse(grepl("_Subgroup\\.", x), sub("_Subgroup\\..*", "", x),
                               sapply(strsplit(x, "_"), function(p) paste(p[-(1:2)], collapse = "_")))
# Broad lineage
lineage_map <- c(
  B.cells = "B cells", B.memory.cells = "B cells", B.naive.cells = "B cells", Plasma = "Plasma cells",
  CAF = "Fibroblasts/CAF", Fibroblasts = "Fibroblasts/CAF", Cancer = "Cancer cells",
  CD4.cells = "CD4 T cells", CD4.memory.activated = "CD4 T cells", CD4.memory.resting = "CD4 T cells",
  CD4.naive = "CD4 T cells", CD4.non.regulatory = "CD4 T cells", T.cells.helper = "CD4 T cells",
  CD4.regulatory = "Tregs", CD8.cells = "CD8 T cells", T.cells.gamma.delta = "gd T cells",
  T.cells.proliferative = "Proliferating T cells", NKT.cells = "NKT cells",
  NK.activated = "NK cells", NK.cells = "NK cells", NK.resting = "NK cells",
  Dendritic.activated.cells = "Dendritic cells", Dendritic.cells = "Dendritic cells",
  Dendritic.resting.cells = "Dendritic cells",
  Macrophages.cells = "Macrophages", Macrophages.M0 = "Macrophages", Macrophages.M1 = "Macrophages",
  Macrophages.M2 = "Macrophages", Monocytes = "Monocytes", Myeloid.cells = "Myeloid cells",
  Mast.cells = "Mast cells", Mast.activated.cells = "Mast cells", Mast.resting.cells = "Mast cells",
  Neutrophils = "Neutrophils", Eosinophils = "Eosinophils",
  Endothelial = "Endothelial cells", Mural.cells = "Mural cells/pericytes", Pericytes = "Mural cells/pericytes",
  Myocytes = "Myocytes")
lab_a <- label_of(cell_a); lab_b <- label_of(cell_b)
stopifnot(all(c(lab_a, lab_b) %in% names(lineage_map)))
lin_a <- lineage_map[lab_a]; lin_b <- lineage_map[lab_b]
# order lineage pair alphabetically (features are direction-merged)
lin_pair <- ifelse(lin_a <= lin_b, paste(lin_a, "<->", lin_b), paste(lin_b, "<->", lin_a))

# ---- 1. cell-type pair level ------------------------------------------------------------
top_n <- 50
rank_in_patient <- t(apply(-feat, 1, rank, ties.method = "min"))
pair_stats <- data.frame(
  feature = colnames(feat), cell_A = cell_a, cell_B = cell_b,
  lineage_A = unname(lin_a), lineage_B = unname(lin_b), lineage_pair = unname(lin_pair),
  median_score = apply(feat, 2, median), mean_score = colMeans(feat),
  sd_score = apply(feat, 2, sd),
  frac_patients_nonzero = colMeans(feat > 0),
  frac_patients_in_top50 = colMeans(rank_in_patient <= top_n),
  median_rank_in_patient = apply(rank_in_patient, 2, median))
pair_stats <- pair_stats[order(-pair_stats$median_score), ]
pair_stats$cohort_rank <- seq_len(nrow(pair_stats))
write.csv(pair_stats, file.path(out_dir, "celltype_pair_statistics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- 2. lineage pair level --------------------------------------------------------------
# Per patient: mean score over all features of that lineage pair; then cohort summaries.
lp_levels <- unique(lin_pair)
lp_patient <- sapply(lp_levels, function(lp) rowMeans(feat[, lin_pair == lp, drop = FALSE]))
lp_rank <- t(apply(-lp_patient, 1, rank, ties.method = "min"))
top100 <- head(pair_stats$feature, 100)
lin_stats <- data.frame(
  lineage_pair = lp_levels,
  n_features = as.integer(table(lin_pair)[lp_levels]),
  median_score = apply(lp_patient, 2, median), mean_score = colMeans(lp_patient),
  frac_patients_in_top10 = colMeans(lp_rank <= 10),
  median_rank_in_patient = apply(lp_rank, 2, median),
  n_features_in_cohort_top100 = sapply(lp_levels, function(lp) sum(lin_pair[match(top100, colnames(feat))] == lp)))
lin_stats <- lin_stats[order(-lin_stats$median_score), ]
write.csv(lin_stats, file.path(out_dir, "lineage_pair_statistics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(lp_patient, file.path(out_dir, "lineage_pair_scores_per_patient.csv"))

# Lineage x lineage heatmap of cohort-median score (log10)
lins <- sort(unique(c(lin_a, lin_b)))
M <- matrix(NA, length(lins), length(lins), dimnames = list(lins, lins))
for (r in seq_len(nrow(lin_stats))) {
  p <- strsplit(lin_stats$lineage_pair[r], " <-> ")[[1]]
  M[p[1], p[2]] <- M[p[2], p[1]] <- lin_stats$median_score[r]
}
pdf(file.path(out_dir, "lineage_pair_heatmap.pdf"), width = 11, height = 10)
pheatmap(log10(M + 1e-6), main = "Gide: median direct communication (log10), lineage pairs",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "orange", "darkred"))(100), na_col = "grey90")
dev.off()

# Top-25 cell-type pairs: per-patient distribution
top25 <- head(pair_stats, 25)
long <- data.frame(feature = rep(top25$feature, each = nrow(feat)),
                   score = as.vector(feat[, top25$feature]))
long$label <- factor(paste(top25$cell_A, "<->", top25$cell_B)[match(long$feature, top25$feature)],
                     levels = rev(paste(top25$cell_A, "<->", top25$cell_B)))
g <- ggplot(long, aes(label, score)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  coord_flip() + scale_y_log10() + theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Direct communication score (log10)", title = "Gide: top 25 cell-type pairs (cohort median)")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "top25_celltype_pairs_boxplot.pdf"), g, width = 11, height = 8)

top15l <- head(lin_stats, 15)
g2 <- ggplot(top15l, aes(reorder(lineage_pair, median_score), median_score)) +

# Summarize ligand-receptor contributions (explain_lr_contributions) of the leading Gide
# cell-type pairs: per edge, which LR pairs carry most of the score and how consistently
# across patients. Run from the results/ directory.
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))

map <- read.csv("sample_id_mapping.csv")
edges <- list.dirs("lr_contributions", recursive = FALSE)
all_top <- list()
for (d in edges) {
  x <- read.csv(file.path(d, "result.csv"))
  x$Patient <- map$original[match(x$Patient, map$racing_id)]
  write.csv(x, file.path(d, "result_original_ids.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  x$LR <- paste(x$Ligand, "->", x$Receptor)
  n_pat <- length(unique(x$Patient))
  # within each patient, rank LR pairs by contribution
  x <- x[order(x$Patient, -x$Contribution), ]
  x$rank <- ave(x$Contribution, x$Patient, FUN = function(v) seq_along(v))
  s <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(x, x$LR), function(g) data.frame(
    LR = g$LR[1], Ligand = g$Ligand[1], Receptor = g$Receptor[1],
    Sender = g$Sender[1], Receiver = g$Receiver[1],
    median_pct_of_edge = median(c(g$PctOfTotal, rep(0, n_pat - nrow(g)))),
    mean_pct_of_edge = sum(g$PctOfTotal) / n_pat,
    frac_patients_top10 = sum(g$rank <= 10) / n_pat,
    frac_patients_present = nrow(g) / n_pat)))
  s <- s[order(-s$mean_pct_of_edge), ]
  s$edge <- basename(d)
  write.csv(s, file.path(d, "lr_pair_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  all_top[[basename(d)]] <- head(s, 10)
  cat("\n==", basename(d), "(", s$Sender[1], "<->", s$Receiver[1], ")  LR pairs:", nrow(s), "\n")
  cat("   top-10 LR pairs cover", round(sum(head(s$mean_pct_of_edge, 10)), 1), "% of the edge on average\n")
  print(head(s[, c("LR", "mean_pct_of_edge", "frac_patients_top10", "frac_patients_present")], 10),
        row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
}
top <- do.call(rbind, all_top)
write.csv(top, "lr_contributions/top10_lr_pairs_per_edge.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# LR pairs recurring among the top 10 of several edges
rec <- aggregate(edge ~ LR, top, function(e) paste(sort(unique(e)), collapse = ";"))
rec$n_edges <- lengths(strsplit(rec$edge, ";"))
rec <- rec[order(-rec$n_edges), ]
write.csv(rec, "lr_contributions/recurrent_lr_pairs_across_edges.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nLR pairs in the top 10 of >= 3 edges:\n"); print(rec[rec$n_edges >= 3, ], row.names = FALSE)

# Ligand / receptor family view across all six edges (mean % of edge)
allsum <- do.call(rbind, lapply(edges, function(d) read.csv(file.path(d, "lr_pair_summary.csv"))))
lig <- aggregate(mean_pct_of_edge ~ Ligand, allsum, sum); lig$mean_pct_of_edge <- lig$mean_pct_of_edge / length(edges)
lig <- lig[order(-lig$mean_pct_of_edge), ]
write.csv(lig, "lr_contributions/ligand_share_across_edges.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nTop ligands (mean % share across the 6 edges):\n"); print(head(lig, 15), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

g <- ggplot(top, aes(reorder(LR, mean_pct_of_edge), mean_pct_of_edge)) + geom_col(fill = "seagreen") +
  coord_flip() + facet_wrap(~edge, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) + theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean % of edge score across patients", title = "Gide: top 10 LR pairs per leading cell-type pair")
ggsave("lr_contributions/top10_lr_pairs_per_edge.pdf", g, width = 12, height = 12)

# Gide cohort – cell-cell communication (RaCInG, kernel method)

Input: `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt` (18,979 genes x 73 pre-treatment samples, log2(TPM+1)).

## Steps
1. `Gide_TPM_linear.csv` – log2(TPM+1) converted back to linear TPM (2^x - 1). RaCInG was run with
   `already_normalized=TRUE`. Sample IDs have an `S` in front because the internal deconvolution
   renamed IDs that start with a digit (`10_PD1_PRE` -> `X10_PD1_PRE`), so they no longer matched the
   expression matrix. `sample_id_mapping.csv` maps them back; all files in `patterns/` and
   `lr_contributions/*/result_original_ids.csv` use the original IDs.
2. `racing_inputs/` – `prepare_racing_inputs`, all defaults: deconvolution with Quantiseq, EpiDISH,
   DeconRNASeq, DWLS and CIBERSORTx, each with all its signatures (raw estimates in
   `Results/Deconvolution_Gide.csv`), then grouping into cell-type subgroups -> 194 cell types,
   661 ligands, 611 receptors, OmniPath ligand-receptor network.
   The first full attempt ran out of memory; the retry (OmniPath network already cached)
   completed, peaking at ~10 GB in use on the machine (`logs/memory_monitor.log`).
3. `racing_kernel/` – `run_racing_kernel`, defaults (raw scores, `norm=FALSE`; directions merged):
   73 patients x 18,767 direct-communication features `Dir_<A>_<B>`.
4. `patterns/` – `scripts/summarize_racing_patterns.R`
   - `celltype_pair_statistics.csv`: per cell-type pair: cohort median/mean score, fraction of
     patients where it is non-zero / in that patient's top 50, median within-patient rank.
   - `lineage_pair_statistics.csv`, `lineage_pair_scores_per_patient.csv`: the same at the level
     of broad cell types (all estimates of one broad cell type pooled, per-patient mean).
   - `lineage_pair_heatmap.pdf`, `top15_lineage_pairs_barplot.pdf`, `top25_celltype_pairs_boxplot.pdf`.
5. `lr_contributions/` – `explain_lr_contributions` for 6 leading cell-type pairs (B<->B, CAF<->B,
   CAF<->CAF, Cancer<->B, Cancer<->Cancer, B<->M1 macrophages), summarised by
   `scripts/summarize_lr_contributions.R`: `*/lr_pair_summary.csv`,
   `top10_lr_pairs_per_edge.csv/.pdf`, `recurrent_lr_pairs_across_edges.csv`,
   `ligand_share_across_edges.csv`.
6. `session_export/` – reproducibility log of every RaCInG tool call.

## Caveat
Raw kernel scores are weighted by cell-type abundance, so the most abundant cell types dominate the
ranking. The three B-cell estimates from the NSCLC-PBMC signature are the most abundant cell types
in this cohort (~5% each). That signature contains only blood cells (no tumor or stromal cells), so
in melanoma tissue those "B cells" probably absorb signal from other cells. The expression profiles
estimated for each cell type are also mixed: e.g. the "B cell" profile expresses myeloid genes
(TYROBP, CD14) and `Cancer_Subgroup.2` expresses T-cell genes (CD3D).

RaCInG has finished on the Gide cohort. The most common pattern is signaling among a handful of very abundant cell types, centred on fibroblasts/CAFs and B cells, with myeloid cells, macrophages and tumor cells next. The B-cell signal looks like an artefact, so treat that part with care. Everything is saved in `results/`, and `results/README.md` explains each folder.

**How I ran it**
- **Input:** the expression file is log2(TPM+1), so I converted it back to linear TPM for RaCInG (`results/Gide_TPM_linear.csv`).
- **Sample IDs:** RaCInG's deconvolution renames IDs that start with a digit (`10_PD1_PRE` becomes `X10_PD1_PRE`), which broke the matching. I put an `S` in front of each ID for the run. The results use your original IDs, and `results/sample_id_mapping.csv` maps between them.
- **Input step** (`results/racing_inputs/`): all default settings, including CIBERSORTx with your credentials. This gave 194 cell types, 661 ligands, 611 receptors and 73 patients. The first full attempt ran out of memory; a plain retry succeeded.
- **Kernel step** (`results/racing_kernel/`): default settings, giving 73 patients × 18,767 cell-type-pair scores.
- **Ligand–receptor breakdown** (`results/lr_contributions/`): I split six of the strongest cell-type pairs into the ligand–receptor pairs behind them.

**Most common cell-type pairs** (`results/patterns/`)

| Broad cell-type pair | Patients where it ranks in their top 10 |
|---|---|
| Fibroblasts/CAF ↔ Fibroblasts/CAF | 92% |
| Fibroblasts/CAF ↔ Myeloid cells | 81% |
| Myeloid cells ↔ Myeloid cells | 70% |
| B cells ↔ Fibroblasts/CAF | 66% |
| Fibroblasts/CAF ↔ Macrophages | 62% |
| B cells ↔ Myeloid cells, Macrophages ↔ Myeloid cells | 58% |
| Fibroblasts/CAF ↔ Monocytes | 49% |

- Tumor cells come next, mainly paired with CAFs and myeloid cells.
- For individual cell types, B cells ↔ B cells, CAF ↔ B cells and CAF ↔ CAF are each in the top 50 for 70–97% of patients.
- Of the 100 strongest individual pairs, B cells ↔ macrophages account for 22, B cells ↔ CAF for 12 and B cells ↔ monocytes for 9.
- The pattern is very consistent: these pairs are non-zero in every patient (97% for the tumor-cell pairs).

**Ligand–receptor pairs behind them**
- **Shared across edges:** APOE→TYROBP and TYROBP→CD44 are in the top 10 of four of the six pairs I broke down. APP→CD74, APP→TYROBP and CLU→TYROBP are in three.
- **CAF ↔ CAF:** CNTN1→NOTCH1, CNTN1→NRCAM, NID1→PTPRF, SLIT2→GPC1, and collagen/SPP1→ITGB1.
- **B cells ↔ M1 macrophages:** CCL2→CCR1 (top 10 in 80% of patients), HLA-A/B/C→LILRA1, IL10→IL10RA and VEGFC→LYVE1.
- **Tumor cells ↔ B cells:** SELPLG→SELL (top 10 in 90% of patients) and HLA-A/B/C/B2M→CD3D.
- **Most-used ligands overall:** APP, COL4A1/COL4A2, SPP1, APOE, VEGFA, LAMA2, THBS1, MDK, TGFB1 and CXCL12. This points to a microenvironment shaped by extracellular matrix, myeloid cells and immune suppression.
- **No single pair dominates:** each edge is spread over 200–770 ligand–receptor pairs, and the top 10 together carry only 2.5–9% of an edge's score.

**Limits on interpretation**
1. **The scores follow cell abundance.** RaCInG's default scores are weighted by how much of each cell type a patient has, so common cell types rank highest.
2. **The "B cells" are probably not real B cells.** The three most abundant cell types (about 5% each) are B-cell estimates from a signature built from lung-cancer patients' blood (NSCLC-PBMC). That signature has no tumor or stromal cells, so in melanoma tissue those "B cells" are likely absorbing signal from other cells.
3. **The estimated expression profiles are mixed.** For example, the "B cell" profile expresses myeloid genes (TYROBP, CD14), and a tumor-cell subgroup expresses a T-cell gene (CD3D). Read ligand–receptor pairs tied to a specific cell type with that in mind.

RaCInG can also score each pair against a baseline that removes the effect of abundance (`norm=True`), which would show which pairs communicate more than their abundance alone predicts. Should I run that version as well?

Everything is in `results/`; open these first:
- `patterns/lineage_pair_statistics.csv`
- `patterns/celltype_pair_statistics.csv`
- `patterns/lineage_pair_heatmap.pdf`
- `lr_contributions/top10_lr_pairs_per_edge.pdf`
- `README.md`

## 1. Input data

- **Transformation:** I converted `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt` from log2(TPM+1) back to linear TPM (2^x − 1, negatives clipped to 0) and saved it as `results/Gide_TPM_linear.csv`.
- **Steps:** this linear TPM was the only expression input, used by `prepare_racing_inputs`. That step does both the deconvolution and the ligand/receptor expression, so both ran on linear TPM.
- **Why:** deconvolution must run on linear TPM, and RaCInG's expression threshold is compared on the linear scale.
- **Scale check:** values ranged 0–14 with no missing values. I only checked the sums of the first 6 samples, which were about 1.3–6.6×10⁵ rather than 10⁶. I did not renormalize or investigate this.
- **Sample IDs:** I added an `S` in front of every ID. This changes no values; `results/sample_id_mapping.csv` maps them back.

## 2. Methods

**Run:**
- RaCInG-server: `start_workflow_session`, `prepare_racing_inputs` (3 attempts, last one succeeded), `get_session_status`, `run_racing_kernel`, `explain_lr_contributions` (6 cell-type pairs), `export_session_results`.
- Two R scripts of my own in `results/scripts/` to rank cell-type pairs and broad cell-type pairs, and to summarise ligand–receptor pairs.

**Skipped:**
- **Monte Carlo method:** the guidance prefers the kernel method, and with 194 cell types Monte Carlo would be very costly. As a result, the network-integration (GSCC) features were not computed.
- **Abundance-normalized kernel (`norm=True`):** it is not the default, so I offered it instead of running it.
- **Ligand–receptor breakdown for other pairs:** I broke down only 6 of the 18,767 pairs. I picked them from the top of the ranking to cover different cell types (ranks 1, 7, 10, 11, 17 and 22), not strictly the top 6.
- **Clinical data:** `data/colData_all.txt` was not used, since no association with response was asked for.

## 3. Parameters

- **RaCInG tools:** I set only what the data or setup required: `already_normalized=true`, the CIBERSORTx email and token, `file_name` and `output_dir`. Everything else stayed at defaults, including all five deconvolution methods.
- **My own choices in the summary scripts:**
  - top-50 and top-10 cutoffs;
  - ranking by cohort median score;
  - a hand-made grouping of cell types into broad types (e.g. CAF and fibroblasts merged);
  - per-patient mean over each broad type's features.

## 4. Problems

1. **Sample-name mismatch** (IDs starting with a digit got an `X` in front): I added the `S` prefix and kept a mapping file.
2. **Out of memory (exit −9) at "Computing L-matrix":** I reported it and offered smaller options. You restated the defaults, so I retried the same call while logging memory, and it succeeded.
   - Peak use was about 10 GB, sampled every 10 seconds, so short peaks could be missed. Swap was nearly full.
   - My explanation (the first-time OmniPath download) is a guess, not verified.
3. **`prepare_racing_inputs` returned "Connection closed":** the R run had actually finished. I confirmed this with `ok: true` in `result_summary.json` and "success" in the session status.
4. **Kernel output too large to return directly:** I read it from the saved file with `jq`.
5. **My ligand–receptor script crashed:** each edge contains both directions, so the same ligand–receptor pair appeared twice per patient. I fixed it by keeping sender→receiver in the grouping.
6. **Memory logger would not stop cleanly:** it took a forced kill, and a defunct process entry remains. It uses no resources.
7. **Unexpected biology:** blood-derived B-cell estimates dominate the ranking. The estimated profiles are mixed (CD3D in a tumor-cell subgroup, TYROBP/CD14 in "B cells"). I reported this as a caveat.

## 5. Checks

- **Input:** dimensions, no missing values, no duplicate genes, value range.
- **Deconvolution:** the cell-type matrix is 73 × 194 and each row sums to 1.
- **Kernel:** the features are 73 × 18,767, and no feature is zero in all patients.
- **Script safeguards:** they stop on error if any feature fails to map to a cell-type pair, any cell type is missing from my broad-type grouping, or any sample ID fails to map back.
- **Not checked:**
  - deconvolution quality (e.g. against marker genes);
  - the ID mapping in the ligand–receptor files (no safeguard there);
  - the PDF plots, which I did not open.

## 6. Limits

- **Abundance bias:** the default raw scores follow cell-type abundance, so common cell types rank highest.
- **B-cell signal:** the leading "B cells" come from a lung-cancer blood (NSCLC-PBMC) signature with no tumor or stromal cells. They are likely absorbing other cells' signal.
- **Mixed profiles:** ligand–receptor assignments to specific cell types are uncertain.
- **Unverified assumptions about the features:**
  - I assumed each feature merges both directions, based on its name structure and the ligand–receptor output; I did not verify this in RaCInG's documentation.
  - 18,767 features is 148 fewer than the 18,915 unordered pairs of 194 cell types. I did not investigate why.
- **Broad-type ranking is biased:** a per-patient mean favours broad types with few features. "Myeloid cells" is a single cell type, while B cells ↔ macrophages averages 342 features.
- **Ligand ranking depends on my choices:** the "most-used ligands" come from the 6 pairs I chose. My reading of it (extracellular matrix, myeloid cells, immune suppression) is an interpretation.
- **No uncertainty estimate:** single kernel estimate, no Monte Carlo, no robustness or association analysis.
- **Your CIBERSORTx token may be in `results/`:** it may appear in plain text in the run records (`manifest.json` and the session log in `session_export/`). I did not check; review those files before sharing `results/`.

# Export existing RaCInG results (Gide) to the standard format in standard/.
# Pure format conversion: no recomputation. Run from the results/ directory.
out <- "standard"
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)

inputs <- readRDS("racing_inputs/result.rds")
kern <- readRDS("racing_kernel/result.rds")
map <- read.csv("sample_id_mapping.csv")
ct <- inputs$celltypes

# Lmatrix/Rmatrix rows are unnamed in result.rds; their order is inputs$celltypes
# (checked against the named copies in racing_inputs/Results/{L,R}matrix_Gide.csv).
long_assign <- function(M, cols, what) {
  stopifnot(nrow(M) == length(ct), ncol(M) == length(cols), all(M %in% c(0, 1)))
  w <- which(M == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
  d <- data.frame(cell_type = ct[w[, 1]], x = cols[w[, 2]])
  names(d)[2] <- what
  d[order(match(d$cell_type, ct), d[[what]]), ]
}
lig <- long_assign(inputs$Lmatrix, inputs$ligands, "ligand")
rec <- long_assign(inputs$Rmatrix, inputs$receptors, "receptor")
write.csv(lig, file.path(out, "ligands.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(rec, file.path(out, "receptors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Kernel features: raw (norm = FALSE) and already undirected (remove_direction = TRUE),
# so only the column names are converted from Dir_<A>_<B> to "<A> - <B>".
feat <- as.matrix(kern$features)
pairs <- expand.grid(i = seq_along(ct), j = seq_along(ct))
key_ab <- paste0("Dir_", ct[pairs$i], "_", ct[pairs$j])
m <- match(colnames(feat), key_ab)
stopifnot(!anyNA(m), !anyDuplicated(m))
new_names <- paste(ct[pairs$i[m]], "-", ct[pairs$j[m]])
# each unordered pair must appear only once
unordered <- paste(pmin(pairs$i[m], pairs$j[m]), pmax(pairs$i[m], pairs$j[m]))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unordered))
patient <- map$original[match(rownames(feat), map$racing_id)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(patient))
di <- data.frame(patient = patient, feat, check.names = FALSE)
